Simmonds, "Tubby" Smith, Laing, Reynolds and many others. Come over next Saturday and enjoy the good-fellowship which is fostered so much on these runs.
High Jump.—1, Wise (BH), 5ft. 1½ins.; 2, Reynolds (Dkg.), 5ft.; 3, Savage (BH), 4ft. 11ins. Long Jump.—1, Read (Dkg.), 18ft.; 2, Carter (Dkg.), 17ft. 0ins.; 3, Simmons (BH), 17ft. 8¼.
Jack Frost beat Reynolds of the Police in the 100 Yards with Stan Botwright third. The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place.
880 Yards : 1 Hayden (H.H.H.), 2 Reynolds (Poly), 3 Bishop (Bel.). 2 mins. 13.6 secs. 1 Mile : 1 Burfitt (Bel.), 2 Ross (H.H.H.), 3 Short (Bel.). 4 mins. 43 secs.

With excellent weather and with such fine runners as the Blackheath trio Reynolds, Piper and Busby and Tom Richards, Paterson and Henning competing, it was generally anticipated that Ballington's record would be in danger, and Reynolds put up a magnificent performance in lowering it by 1 min. 20 sec…
Mel Thorpe,running in Belgrave colours for the first time on the Brighton road,was faced with the problem of dealing with Reynolds of Portsmouth and John Snowden of Surrey.
Chris did not let the side down and, against the form book, took 13 seconds off Portsmouth's Reynolds, thus setting up our last two runners for a deserved victory.
John Mitchell had to wait until Heat 6 for his stint knowing that Piggot and Reynolds were dangerous opposition but knowing little of the South African T.

200m: John Mitchell ran a fine race, although the class of internationals Reynolds (TVH) and Knowles told at the end. 400m: Mel Ford beat 50 seconds twice in heat and final, eventually finishing a close-up third.
Just back from injury, JIM VIVIAN splits Knowles (Brighton & H.) and Reynolds (TVH) in the Brockman 100. But he was unable to recover his old dash in time for the A.A.A.
